aspects.says: An epoch number carries no unit: reading seconds with ofEpochMilli (or millis as seconds) gives a valid but wrong instant, and nothing throws.
basis: section:An Instant Is Seconds and Nanoseconds Counted From 1970-01-01T00:00Z

aspects.says: Wall-clock text without an offset becomes an instant only through the sender's zone; appending Z reads it as UTC and shifts it by the zone's offset.
basis: section:Instant.parse Accepts Only Text That Names Its Offset

aspects.says: A month is added to an instant in the customer's zone and converted back; 30 days or UTC give a different moment.
basis: section:An Instant Has No Calendar, So Months Need a Zone

aspects.says: Instant supports units up to DAYS (86,400 s); MONTHS and YEARS and calendar fields throw UnsupportedTemporalTypeException.
basis: section:An Instant Has No Calendar, So Months Need a Zone

aspects.says: Truncating stamps further than the store needs, to seconds, gives two versions in the same second the same stamp, so a stale edit passes the check.
basis: section:A Timestamp Survives a Store Only at the Store's Precision

aspects.says: Instant.now() on Java 21 on Linux fills digits below the millisecond; the javadoc promises only the best available clock.
basis: section:A Timestamp Survives a Store Only at the Store's Precision

aspects.says: Instant.parse accepts text with Z or a numeric offset, converting the offset to UTC, and refuses text without one.
basis: section:Instant.parse Accepts Only Text That Names Its Offset

aspects.says: An Instant is epoch seconds plus a nanosecond part that is never negative, so an instant before 1970 has negative seconds and a positive nano part.
basis: section:An Instant Is Seconds and Nanoseconds Counted From 1970-01-01T00:00Z

aspects.says: An instant written to a millisecond store and read back is unequal to the original unless it was truncated to milliseconds when stamped.
basis: section:A Timestamp Survives a Store Only at the Store's Precision
